text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A cooperation agreement between Bosnian Serb republic and Federal Republic of Yugoslavia is contrary to the Dayton peace agreement and it shows that Belgrade has not given up its ambitions in Bosnia, Moslem chairman of Bosnian collective presidency Alija Izetbegovic and co-chairman of Bosnia's council of ministers Haris Silajdzic say in a statement.

- French citizen Lionel Dumont, suspected of murder of a Bosnian policeman in Zenica, drove into a NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) base in the Sarajevo suburb of Ilidza as he was being chased by Bosnian police, interior ministry spokesman claims. SFOR denies the allegation.
- The fight for an independent Bosnia has always been a fight for democracy, human rights and liberties, Izetbegovic says at a reception marking the fifth aniversary of Bosnia's independence.

- An unmanned NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) reconnaissance plane crashes in southern Bosnia in a routine mission, SFOR says. Damage caused by the incident was minimal because the plane fell in a field.

- The dispute over a common currency in Bosnia will probably be resolved in a month and half time, Serb co-chairman in Bosnia's council of ministers Boro Bosic says in the first interview by a Serb official with media in Moslem-Croat federation. --Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
